about: The one schema of what ABI v1 lets a person choose (T17b). tools/generate_options.py validates it and generates adapters/libretro/options_generated.h
and config/schema/options_table.generated.json; tests/config compares what headless, the libretro core and the BizHawk wrapper use with it.
Never edit the generated files by hand: change this file and run python3 tools/generate_options.py.
class 'reboot': part of the machine. It maps to a p6_config field, so it enters config_hash and the state identity; a change needs a reload and
never moves the running machine or the state bound. class 'presentation': no effect on emulation; it is applied in place.
Only what the ABI honours is here (bridge/config.cpp validate_config). The CPU, the RAM and the ROM are not choices: they are listed under
'unsupported' with the reason, which is the diagnostic a request for them gets. The machine is a choice between the presets the ABI has (T23d, T24e):
the A500 (OCS, 512 KiB Chip + 512 KiB Slow, Kickstart 1.3), the A600 (ECS, 1 MiB Chip, no Slow RAM, Kickstart 2.05, without Gayle: no IDE and no PCMCIA)
and the A1200 (68EC020, AGA, 2 MiB Chip, no Slow or Fast RAM, Kickstart 3.1, without Gayle).
PUAE5 (libretro-uae) calls it puae_model: its A500 is this A500, but its A600 is a Kickstart 3.1 machine with 2 MiB Chip + 8 MiB Fast, which this one is not;
its A1200OG (2 MiB Chip) is this A1200, while its A1200 carries 8 MiB of Fast RAM (task T49). So the key is puae6_machine, with the values of the ABI, and no PUAE5 key is read.
A value may carry "wrapper": false: the libretro core and headless offer it but the BizHawk wrapper does not yet (its sync setting enum lacks it); the A1200 until T24f.

categories.label: Machine
categories.info: What the emulated Amiga is. These options take effect when the content is loaded.

categories.label: Video
categories.info: How the picture is presented. These options apply at once.

values.label: A500 (OCS, 512 KiB Chip + 512 KiB Slow, Kickstart 1.3)
A600 (ECS, 1 MiB Chip, Kickstart 2.05, no IDE or PCMCIA)
A1200 (68EC020, AGA, 2 MiB Chip, no Gayle)

libretro.label: Model
libretro.info: The A500 is the OCS machine with Kickstart 1.3; the A600 is the ECS machine with 1 MiB of Chip RAM and Kickstart 2.05; the A1200 is the AGA machine with a 68EC020 (cycle exact), 2 MiB of Chip RAM and Kickstart 3.1 (PUAE5's A1200OG). The A600 and the A1200 have no IDE or PCMCIA: Gayle is not emulated. The Kickstart is looked for in the system directory under the names of the chosen model (A500: kick34005.A500, A600: kick37350.A600, A1200: kick40068.A1200).

libretro.label: Video Standard
libretro.info: PAL has 312 lines at 50 Hz and NTSC 262 lines at 60 Hz. It decides the clock and the timing of the whole machine.

libretro.label: Audio Sample Rate
libretro.info: The rate Paula's output is produced at. The count of audio frames of every unit follows the emulated clock at this rate.

options.libretro_policy: Fixed at the default. A seed picked from a menu is a way to make two sessions of the same content differ for no reason a person can see; the seed belongs to whoever records or replays (headless --seed, the wrapper's sync settings).
Fixed at the default (2000-01-01T00:00:00Z). The clock never follows the host, and a date typed into a menu is the same hazard as a seed; the wrapper keeps it in the movie's sync settings.

libretro.label: Aspect Ratio
libretro.info: The aspect ratio announced to the frontend: the one the pixels of the chosen video standard have, or a plain 4:3. The picture itself is not changed.

reserved.why: How many of the given disks start in a drive is a media placement made with media events (DF0 and DF1 exist in the bridge); libretro drives DF0 alone from Disk Control, so there is nothing to offer yet.

unsupported.why: The 68000 at the A500 clock is the only CPU the generated tables cover.
ABI v1 fixes 512 KiB of Chip RAM.
ABI v1 fixes 512 KiB of Slow RAM.
The A500 profile has no Fast RAM.
The Kickstart is given as bytes at load and identified by its content, never chosen by a path in the configuration.
Turbo floppy would change the timing of the machine; the profile fixes the real drive speed.
The machine runs at its real clock; the host speed never changes the emulation.
The deterministic profile has no JIT.
A whole .uae file is not imported; only the keys of this schema are accepted.

The device of a port is input, not configuration: the libretro core offers its types with SET_CONTROLLER_INFO and reads the one chosen with retro_set_controller_port_device at every run (T17c), and the wrapper's ControllerPort1 is a per-session choice; it is not a p6_config field and never enters config_hash.
